Restrict to the 64-bit (x86_64/aarch64) syscall table — kernels that support both need a matching rule per arch so a 32-bit binary can't bypass a 64-bit-only rule.
Audit the system call: `chroot` (change a process's apparent filesystem root).

...where the login/audit UID (auid) is ≥ 1000 — auid tracks the *original* logged-in user even through su/sudo, so this is what actually attributes an action to a person rather than to whatever account a process is currently running as. 1000 is RHEL's default UID_MIN (first normal, non-system account); check /etc/login.defs rather than assuming it on a given host.
...and the login/audit UID (auid) is actually set — excludes processes with no attributable login session.
